title: Custom AST-Based Postal Code Formatter
pattern: Building a custom abstract syntax tree (AST) and interpreter to validate standard, simple structured formats (such as postal codes or phone numbers).
why_bad: It incurs high cognitive overhead and code footprint to perform validations that are solved in a few lines by optimized regular expressions or compiled libraries.
detection: Custom tokenizing, parsing, and AST evaluation methods written locally inside simple format-validation helper modules.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. If the format rules are complex, vary dynamically at runtime based on market localization, or are defined entirely by non-programming users.
source: [2nd] Andrew Hunt_ David Hurst Thomas - _The Pragmatic Programmer_ Your Journey to Mastery_, 20th Anniversary Edition (2019, Addison-Wesley Professional).pdf, Topic 28 "Domain Languages"; Joshua Kerievsky - _Refactoring to Patterns_ (2004, Addison-Wesley Professional).pdf, Chapter 7 "Replace Implicit Language with Interpreter".
